summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing confidential supply-chain data and building a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier actions, approval UI) plus pitch/hand-in materials.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch (art books overbooked 80,000 vs 8,000, failed statue lot, game-card shortfall) and built a working app (poller, versioned store, case/approval UI, routines, sent-folder duplicate guard, drop drill fixes, confirmed-orders-as-inbound). The Nowak art book order was confirmed by email; about 18 commits on jonas/today-flow remain unpushed and README/demo/video are still missing.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks; files are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 checksums, not just filenames.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed with an empty token.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files changed during the turn; 'no files modified' skips checkpointing, and the transcript is still collected in .entire/metadata.

The app only sees emails it sends itself; a shared mailbox means manual sends are invisible unless the sent folder is read and matched (thread reference, then supplier plus PO number, or a unique part number).
Two modules wrote the same impacts.json with different shapes (list vs keyed by event), which crashed the whole pipeline; the predictor now writes event_impacts.json.
Supplier profile JSON addresses were all trusted as send targets; new contacts must now be confirmed by a person before use.
The team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; claim tasks in PROGRESS.md before building.
Replies to side emails must not mark a case as 'sent'; this had silently removed three cases from 'Needs you'.

Routine option matching searched for a literal string including a comma instead of AND-matching terms, so the routine found the right case but sent nothing; routines also mark cases 'seen' on first run so they will not retry.

code.finding: New module that syncs the shared mailbox's sent folder, assigns outgoing mails to cases, and drives the 12-hour duplicate-send guard (409 unless 'Send anyway').
Routine diagram rewritten as three node types (When, one 'Only if' node with numbered list and funnel counts, one node per Then step) on a dotted canvas.
Computes per-condition 'N left' counts in the browser by copying routines.py matching logic; approximate for waiting and replies triggers.
Compares newer supplier profiles against profile.csv and raises cards (e.g. PackRight at risk, Pune qualification expired 30 Oct).
Imports supplier_master; commit b0cff82 accidentally included api.py edits without that untracked file, making that commit alone unstartable until fixed.

workflow: Subagents are effective for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations vs SAP, 59 scans) and for UX review with screenshots taken on a copy of state with background jobs off.
Rehearse drops on a copy of data/state with ASK_REPLY_POLL=off, ASK_TEAMS=off, ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none so nothing polls the real portal, sends mail or places calls.
Use git status checks and split commits by topic when parallel agents leave uncommitted work, to avoid one commit picking up another's changes.
Verify UI fixes in the browser (press J seven times, measure scroll position) before committing.

friction: Portal token was empty initially, blocking data access until the user supplied it.
The art book order went out twice (in-app at 06:50 and by hand at 07:04 signed Paul Winter) because the mailbox is shared and the app could not see manual sends.
Pulse test emails to Hwaseong bounced or were stray; the note to Hwaseong and the message to Lucas are still unsent.
Commit b0cff82 accidentally swept in another engineer's uncommitted api.py changes.
Routine toggled on sometimes showed 'not run yet' and did not run; one routine ran but sent nothing due to the option-matching bug.
UI bugs in the Today list: 'Decided by you' click scrolled the list to top, and the left list did not scroll with selection.
Unclear whether portal data is identical across teams or whether supplier actions change portal data.
Karton's art books likely arrive about 19:30, but the Collector's cell runs out at about 11:16.
